draft.title: The Crusades
card: The Crusades were a series of wars that began in 1095. Christian armies from Europe fought Muslim rulers for control of Jerusalem, a city holy to Christians, Muslims and Jews.
The Pope called for the first Crusade. Many people joined because of their religious faith. Others hoped for land, wealth or status.
The wars caused many deaths on both sides. Cities were attacked and many people were killed or driven from their homes.
Contact with the Muslim world also brought new trade goods and ideas to Europe. Spices and silks were traded, and European scholars learned new knowledge.
draft.remember: The Crusades were religious wars over Jerusalem that caused great loss of life and also opened Europe to new trade and ideas.

a.q: What was the main aim of the Christian armies that set out in 1095?
opts: To take control of Jerusalem from Muslim rulers
To end a plague that was spreading across Europe
To force the English king to obey the law
To drive the English out of France
a.why: The Crusades began as a fight for control of Jerusalem, which Muslim rulers held. The plague, the limit on the king and the war in France belong to other events, not to the Crusades.
a.clue: Think about which city the card says the wars were fought over.

b.q: Tomas is a merchant in a European port in 1250. His trade in spices and silks has grown since the Crusades began. What does this show about the Crusades?
opts: They brought Europe new trade as well as deaths
They ended the fighting between Christians and Muslims
They gave Europeans no contact with the Muslim world
They brought only suffering and no lasting change
b.why: Tomas's growing trade shows that contact with the Muslim world brought Europe new goods. The wars also caused many deaths, so the effects were mixed. Saying they brought only suffering ignores the trade and ideas that also came to Europe.
b.clue: The Crusades had more than one kind of effect.

a.best: To take control of Jerusalem from Muslim rulers

b.best: They brought Europe new trade as well as deaths

problems.detail: The question says the Christian armies 'set out in 1095'. Pope Urban II called the First Crusade in November 1095, but the armies did not leave until 1096. It would be accurate to say 'the Crusade called in 1095' or 'the armies that set out in 1096'.
